findings.evidence: Capture report inline_finding B-S1-PILL-2 (severity P0): capture.json initial_server_statuses = {"70": 8, "72": 7} — order #70 (the delivery order seeded for Wave T) arrived at KDS already at status=8 (READY/Prête) BEFORE any chef bump, instead of status=7 (PREPARING/En cours). Wave S-1 backend auto-transition ACCEPT→PREPARING regressed for at least the delivery-order branch of the seeder. Cross-checked in screenshot 02: card A0002 (with delivery block '12 rue Test, Paris 75001 / Wave T E2E 1779300395176 / 0612345678') shows the green 'PRÊTE' pill (rgb 16,185,129) in the kds-card__state-pill — NOT the blue 'EN COURS' pill it should display. Validations block of capture.json: 'S-1_auto_preparing': 'FAIL'. This violates the user-facing contract closed by Wave S-1 (task #114). Production impact: chef sees 'Prête' before they actually prepared the order; the order would be served raw or skipped. Fiscal/business invariant: PREPARING→READY transition must be chef-initiated for delivery orders so the timestamp captured in audit log truly reflects food readiness, not just paid status. NF525 chain still bit-identical (count=18, last_hash=1e2762af… pre==post) so audit-log integrity is intact — but the FACT recorded for #70 is wrong.
findings.fix_hint: Investigate Wave S-1 auto-PREPARING listener. Likely root cause: delivery-channel orders (channel='delivery' or order_type=DELIVERY) skip the ACCEPT→PREPARING transition because the seeder/factory inserts at fiscal_status=READY directly OR the listener guard condition (e.g. payment_method=='cash_on_delivery') exits early. Re-examine app/Listeners/OrderAcceptedAutoPreparing.php (or equivalent) and the Wave T seeder tests/e2e/__fixtures__/wave-t-orders.json composition. If the seeder is the cause (fixture sets status=8 directly), fix the fixture so order_2 is created at status=6 (CONFIRMED) and lets the listener promote it to status=7 (PREPARING) — that's what the spec is meant to verify. If the listener is the cause, branch on order_type to include DELIVERY.

findings.evidence: Capture report says order_1_id=72 + order_2_id=70 (2 orders created by the Wave T seeder), but DOM state 02..08 contain THREE cards in the V2 grid: aria-label='Commande A0002' (with the wave-t delivery block — backend id=70), 'Commande A0003' (backend id=72), 'Commande A0004' (UNKNOWN backend id, NOT created by this run). Card A0004 has identical body content to A0003 ('Sandwich Cayenne / Tacos / Coca-Cola 33cl') and identical CAISSE source chip — it is a STALE order from a prior Wave S or Wave T-R1 run that was not cleaned up by the spec's DB reset hook. State 08 shows BOTH original orders bumped (A0002 + A0004 turn 'Prête') but A0003 remains 'En cours' — meaning the spec bumped the WRONG order #72 (rendered as A0003) and the second bump click landed on the stale A0004 instead of the real delivery order A0002. The capture's server_statuses_post_bump shows {70:8, 72:8} correctly for the two real orders so the backend wasn't fooled, but the visual capture is misleading and any reviewer reading screenshots in isolation would draw wrong conclusions about per-card behaviour.
findings.fix_hint: tests/e2e/test-e2e-wave-t-caisse-to-delivered-B-kds.spec.js — before seeding the 2 Wave T orders, delete any KDS-active orders for branch_id=1 created in the last 24h, e.g. via beforeAll Artisan command 'kds:reset-active-orders --branch=1 --since=24h' or direct DB DELETE. Otherwise stale orders from sibling Wave S/T-R1 specs pollute the visual capture and obscure which card maps to which fresh fixture id. Recommend also adding data-testid='kds-v2-card-order-{id}' on each card so adversarial reviewers can DOM-grep for the exact backend id rather than queue-letter aliases.
